rows.consequence: A self-consistent artifact containing fabricated low-variance observations can understate the active floor, suppress effect_not_above_floor, and permit a direction-supported claim whose detection-floor premise is not evidence-bound. This is claim invalidation.
rows.counterevidence: The artifact validator enforces schema, finite hashes, uniqueness, internal arithmetic, eligibility, and provenance-list consistency; the loader hashes the artifact file, strict-validates consumer bundles, and binds their config identities. Those controls detect malformed artifacts but do not prove that the stored floor measurements came from the named bundle bytes.
evidence_refs: joulewise/detection_floor.py:14-18 explicitly states that v1 does not bind provenance to bundle bytes or the frozen order log and is not claim-consumable until that binding lands.
joulewise/detection_floor.py:751-806 recomputes floor arithmetic solely from the artifact's own metric_value_j values and checks bundle_sha256 only for hexadecimal shape.
joulewise/analysis_engine/inputs.py:203-208 loads a floor after validate_floor_artifact only.
joulewise/analysis_engine/inputs.py:1227-1285 resolves an exact cell using consumer_pairs.issubset(source_pairs), where both sets contain only bundle_id and config_sha256.
joulewise/analysis_engine/__init__.py:271-304 gives declared exact resolution priority over transport resolution.
joulewise/analysis_engine/claims.py:197-268 uses floor_gate_j directly when deciding effect_not_above_floor and the supported outcome.
tests/test_analysis_integration.py:360-450 changes only fixture bundle_id and config_sha256 values, then asserts that all gross floors resolve exact.
tests/test_detection_floor.py:278-337 (cross-boundary helper) shows those test cells retain fixture metric values and constant synthetic bundle_sha256 values.

Bounded absence search across detection_floor.py, analysis_engine/inputs.py, analysis_engine/__init__.py, and test_analysis_integration.py found no consumer comparison for observation bundle_sha256 or metric_value_j.
rows.finding: An artifact can resolve as an exact claim floor without binding its bundle_sha256 values or metric_value_j observations to the referenced bundle bytes or summary metrics. Exact resolution matches only telemetry/metric/window/condition plus a subset of (bundle_id, config_sha256) pairs.

rows.consequence: The near-floor branch of the frozen design cannot be represented by the canonical campaign-to-analysis flow. Campaign scale-up would require bypassing or forking the generator and validator, making the next roadmap gate unsafe and non-reproducible.

rows.consequence: A campaign member can remain collection-usable even though expected prompt-token hashes are unavailable. Corpus provenance therefore downgrades according to incidental filesystem shape instead of producing an explicit missing-evidence flag.

ID-native prompts also carry token IDs directly and do not need this text-tokenization comparison.

rows.consequence: A strict-invalid or claim-unready intermediate bundle can be presented as a JouleWise run report. If the report is reused as a reader-facing surface, its token metric violates the binding primary-metric and stack-identity rules and can be mistaken for publishable evidence.
rows.counterevidence: The module describes itself as a run browser rather than a formal claim artifact, exposes full raw metadata and summary details, and omits the chart when the reducer-compatible power curve is unreadable. Its actual publication use was not established.

rows.finding: The generic HTML report treats any parseable summary as complete, renders raw metadata and summary values without strict-bundle or claim-verdict gates, and headlines energy/token without co-displaying request energy, tokenizer identity, or measurement boundary.

rows.consequence: Dataset consumers can treat a planned cap as realized evidence, particularly for early stops or failures, and may recompute or audit token denominators using false provenance.
rows.counterevidence: The actual energy_output_token_j metric is read from reducer output, whose denominator logic refuses config fallback; the figure and table label it runtime-observed, retain token_count_source, and explicitly downgrade the legacy evidence. The audited bundles were not in scope, so configured and realized counts may coincide for these fixed-budget runs.
